title: One millilitre of steam
hook: Boil a single millilitre of water. How much room does the steam need?

knows: that water boils to steam at 100 °C
doesNotKnow: that boiling spreads the same molecules into about 1,600 times the space

misconception: Gas molecules are bigger, or steam is just hot water taking about the same room.
objective: The learner can explain that 1 mL of water at 100 °C and 1 atm becomes about 1,630 mL of steam (ideal gas), because the same molecules move far apart, not because they grow.

claims.text: 1 mL of liquid water at 100 °C boils to about 1,630 mL of steam at 1 atm, treating steam as an ideal gas: about 1,600 times the room.
claims.source: n = 0.9584 g / 18.015 g/mol = 0.05320 mol; V = nRT/p = 0.05320 x 0.082057 x 373.15 / 1 = 1.629 L (node; Demo.tsx STEAM_ML). Liquid density at 100 °C 0.9584 g/mL (CRC Handbook, 'Properties of water').

claims.text: Real steam at 100 °C and 1 atm takes about 2% less room than the ideal-gas value.
claims.source: Steam tables (IAPWS-IF97): saturated vapour at 100 °C, 101.4 kPa, specific volume 1.672 m3/kg, so 0.9584 g gives about 1,603 mL, 1.6% below 1,629 mL. Published expansion ratios about 1,600 to 1,700. · Fact-check 2026-10-13: Steam table 1.672 m3/kg x 0.9584 g = 1.602 L, 1.6% below ideal; "about 2%" is fair.

claims.text: Boiling does not make molecules bigger or change them; in the liquid they touch their neighbours, and in steam each has on average about 1,600 times as much space, so the gas is mostly empty.
claims.source: Kinetic-molecular picture of liquids and gases (Atkins & Jones, Chemical Principles, ch. on gases and liquids). The H2O molecule is the same in both phases.

claims.text: Steam is invisible until it cools into droplets.
claims.source: Water vapour is a transparent gas; the visible 'steam' above a kettle is condensed droplets (Atkins & Jones; any meteorology text on condensation).

claims.text: The stage is a drawing: 30 molecules stand for the whole millilitre, volume is on a log scale, and gas positions are a fixed scatter (mulberry32 seed 7, layout only, not evidence).
claims.source: Demo.tsx N_MOL, Y(), SPOTS. A free piston at 1 atm means the volume at each boiled share is (1 - f) x 1 mL + f x 1,629 mL.

recall.question: A sealed 1 L bottle holds a few drops of water. You heat it until all the water is steam. Why does the bottle risk bursting?
options: the steam needs far more room than the liquid did
recall.why: The same molecules spread out: at 1 atm a millilitre of water needs about 1,600 mL as steam, so in a fixed bottle the pressure climbs instead.
